correctness.rationale: For distinct positive susceptibility nodes, a positive truncated Vandermonde moment fiber is one-dimensional with barycentric weights b_i. The highest moment difference equals its unique scalar coefficient. The (k-1)-st derivative of 1-exp(-zx) has strict sign (-1)^k at positive pressure; the divided-difference mean-value formula gives strict all-pressure ordering. Positive pressure roots exist and are unique by strict concavity, and their monotone attack-fraction maps inherit the order. The binary-C construction keeps both full marginals and all lower moments fixed with last moment difference 4 a epsilon. The k=3 witness is exact and the standalone checker verified rational identities for 3<=k<=10 plus example roots; no finite check is used as proof for all k.

value.rationale: The origin paper motivates the inadequacy of covariance to order epidemics under joint susceptibility--infectivity dependence. For a natural population with k known risk classes, this theorem gives the precise minimal mixed-moment information sufficient for deterministic final-size computation and a universal odd/even order rule when all lower moments agree. The every-k sharpness even with identical full marginals and equal reproduction threshold demonstrates that the unknown information actually changes epidemic size, rather than merely changing a formal parameter. This resolves a model-specific identifiability/comparison gap; no general downstream theorem is asserted.
